## What This File Is

A Quarto document: ordinary text with pieces of code embedded in it. Press the
Render button above and Quarto runs the code, drops the results into the text,
and writes `report.html` next to this file.

The point is that the numbers below are not typed in. They are computed from
`quarterly_revenue.csv`, which sits in this same folder. Edit the CSV, render
again, and every figure, table, and sentence updates itself.

```{python}
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("quarterly_revenue.csv")
df["margin"] = df["margin"] / 100
df
```

## Revenue

```{python}
#| label: fig-revenue
#| fig-cap: "Quarterly revenue and cost, in millions of dollars."

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
ax.bar(df["quarter"], df["revenue"], color="#00205B", label="Revenue")
ax.bar(df["quarter"], df["cost"], color="#f59e0b", width=0.5, label="Cost")
ax.set_ylabel("$ millions")
ax.legend(frameon=False)
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha="right")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
first, last = df.iloc[0], df.iloc[-1]
growth = (last["revenue"] / first["revenue"] - 1) * 100
```

Revenue grew from `{python} f"${first['revenue']:.2f}M"` in
`{python} first["quarter"]` to `{python} f"${last['revenue']:.2f}M"` in
`{python} last["quarter"]`, an increase of
`{python} f"{growth:.0f}%"` over `{python} len(df)` quarters.

Those numbers are written as inline code, not as text. @fig-revenue is
cross-referenced the same way --- renumber the figures and the reference
follows.

## Margin

Margin has been steady, averaging
`{python} f"{df['margin'].mean():.1%}"` and never leaving the range
`{python} f"{df['margin'].min():.1%}"` to `{python} f"{df['margin'].max():.1%}"`.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Summary by year."

summary = (
    df.assign(year=df["quarter"].str[:4])
      .groupby("year")
      .agg(revenue=("revenue", "sum"),
           cost=("cost", "sum"),
           margin=("margin", "mean"))
      .round(3)
)
summary.style.format({"revenue": "${:.2f}M", "cost": "${:.2f}M", "margin": "{:.1%}"})
```

The fourth quarter is the strongest in both years, which is worth keeping in
mind before reading much into any single quarter against the one before it.

## Math

Inline math like $\pi r^2$ works, and so do displayed equations:

$$
\text{margin}_t = \frac{\text{revenue}_t - \text{cost}_t}{\text{revenue}_t}
$$

The same source produces other formats without editing the text. Change the

## If Rendering Fails

Running Python chunks takes four packages: `jupyter` and `nbformat` for Quarto
to talk to Python at all, plus `pandas` and `matplotlib` for the code here.
`No module named 'nbformat'` is the usual first error.

Ask Claude to install what is missing --- that is a fair test of everything in
this session. Or delete the code chunks and render the prose alone, which needs
nothing beyond Quarto.
